arxiv-2108-06017.title: AGKD-BML: Defense Against Adversarial Attack by Attention Guided Knowledge Distillation and Bi-directional Metric Learning
arxiv-2108-06017.creator: Hong Wang, Yuefan Deng, Shinjae Yoo, Haibin Ling, Yuewei Lin
arxiv-2108-06017.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hong Wang, Yuefan Deng, Shinjae Yoo, Haibin Ling, Yuewei Lin. While deep neural networks have shown impressive performance in many tasks, they are fragile to carefully designed adversarial attacks. We propose a novel adversarial training-based model by Attention Guided Knowledge Distillation and Bi-directional Metric Learning (AGKD-BML).

arxiv-2111-03706.title: Learn one size to infer all: Exploiting translational symmetries in delay-dynamical and spatio-temporal systems using scalable neural networks
arxiv-2111-03706.creator: Mirko Goldmann, Claudio R. Mirasso, Ingo Fischer, Miguel C. Soriano
arxiv-2111-03706.description: Abstract We design scalable neural networks adapted to translational symmetries in dynamical systems, capable of inferring untrained high-dimensional dynamics for different system sizes. We train these networks to predict the dynamics of delay-dynamical and spatio-temporal systems for a single size. Then, we drive the networks by their own predictions.

arxiv-2112-10770.title: Implications of the conformal Higgs model
arxiv-2112-10770.creator: R. K. Nesbet
arxiv-2112-10770.description: Abstract The postulate of universal local Weyl scaling (conformal) symmetry modifies both general relativity and the Higgs scalar field model. The conformal Higgs model (CHM) acquires a cosmological effect that fits observed accelerating Hubble expansion for redshifts z ≤ 1 z\leq 1 (7.33 Gyr) accurately with only one free constant parameter.

arxiv-2305-14527.title: Slovo: Russian Sign Language Dataset
arxiv-2305-14527.creator: Kapitanov Alexander, Kvanchiani Karina, Nagaev Alexander, Petrova Elizaveta
arxiv-2305-14527.description: Abstract One of the main challenges of the sign language recognition task is the difficulty of collecting a suitable dataset due to the gap between hard-of-hearing and hearing societies. In addition, the sign language in each country differs significantly, which obliges the creation of new data for each of them.

arxiv-2410-03283.title: From Operator Product Expansion to Anomalous Dimensions
arxiv-2410-03283.creator: Rijun Huang, Qingjun Jin, and Yi Li
arxiv-2410-03283.description: Abstract We propose a new method for computing the renormalization functions, which is based on the ideas of operator product expansion and large momentum expansion. In this method, the renormalization Z Z -factors are determined by the ultraviolet finiteness of Wilson coefficients in the dimensional regularization scheme.

arxiv-2508-06905.title: MultiRef: Controllable Image Generation with Multiple Visual References Conference: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 27–31, 2025; Dublin, Ireland Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’25), October 27–31, 2025, Dublin, Irela
arxiv-2508-06905.creator: Ruoxi Chen, Dongping Chen †, Siyuan Wu, Sinan Wang, Shiyun Lang, Peter Sushko, Gaoyang Jiang, Yao Wan, Ranjay Krishna*
arxiv-2508-06905.description: Abstract . Visual designers naturally draw inspiration from multiple visual references, combining diverse elements and aesthetic principles to create artwork. However, current image generative frameworks predominantly rely on single-source inputs - either text prompts or individual reference images. In this paper, we focus on the task of controllable image generation using multiple visual references.

arxiv-2510-09770.title: Gold Panning : Turning Positional Bias into Signal for Multi-Document LLM Reasoning
arxiv-2510-09770.creator: Adam Byerly, Daniel Khashabi
arxiv-2510-09770.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Adam Byerly, Daniel Khashabi. Large language models exhibit a strong position bias in multi-document contexts, systematically prioritizing information based on location rather than relevance. While existing approaches treat this bias as noise to be mitigated, we introduce Gold Panning Bandits , a framework that leverages position bias as a diagnostic signal: by reordering documents and observing shifts in the model’s responses, we can efficiently identify the most relevant content. We frame the problem of choosing reorderings as a bipartite matching problem.

pmc-10523663.title: Phylogenetic analysis of museum specimens of houting Coregonus oxyrinchus shows the need for a revision of its extinct status
pmc-10523663.creator: R Kroes, Y Winkel, J A J Breeuwer, E E van Loon, S P Loader, J S Maclaine, P F M Verdonschot, H G van der Geest
pmc-10523663.description: According to the IUCN Red List the anadromous houting Coregonus oxyrinchus is categorized as ‘extinct’. However, this extinct status might be incorrect because taxonomic difference between C. oxyrinchus and the closely related C. lavaretus is based on a disputable morphological comparison. Also, phylogenetic studies on mtDNA only focused on recent obtained coregonids.

pmc-10669013.title: Optimizing Image Classification: Automated Deep Learning Architecture Crafting with Network and Learning Hyperparameter Tuning
pmc-10669013.creator: Koon Meng Ang, Wei Hong Lim, Sew Sun Tiang, Abhishek Sharma, Marwa M Eid, Sayed M Tawfeek, Doaa Sami Khafaga, Amal H Alharbi, Abdelaziz A Abdelhamid, Yongquan Zhou, Huajuan Huang, Guo Zhou
pmc-10669013.description: This study introduces ETLBOCBL-CNN, an automated approach for optimizing convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures to address classification tasks of varying complexities. ETLBOCBL-CNN employs an effective encoding scheme to optimize network and learning hyperparameters, enabling the discovery of innovative CNN structures. To enhance the search process, it incorporates a competency-based learning concept inspired by mixed-ability classrooms during the teacher phase.

pmc-11491761.title: Endocapillary proliferative glomerulonephritis associated with Q fever endocarditis: A case report
pmc-11491761.creator: Craig Peter Coorey, William James, Venkat Manickavasagam, Jason Chen, Sanjeev Baweja
pmc-11491761.description: Key Clinical MessageAcute Coxiella burnetti (Q fever) infection is known to activate the autoimmune inflammatory response. We report a rare case of glomerulonephritis associated with the Coxiella infection. An elderly male first presented with recurrent fevers of unknown origin and was subsequently diagnosed with Q fever infection and treated with doxycycline.

pmc-11718521.title: Proposed computed tomography severity index for the evaluation of invasive fungal sinusitis: Preliminary results
pmc-11718521.creator: Smita Manchanda, Ashu S Bhalla, Ankita D Nair, Kapil Sikka, Hitesh Verma, Alok Thakar, Aanchal Kakkar, Maroof A Khan
pmc-11718521.description: BACKGROUNDInvasive fungal sinusitis (IFS) can present as a mild disease to life-threatening infection. A recent surge in cases was seen due to the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Many patients require surgical debridement and hence imaging [contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) of the paranasal sinuses (PNS)] to document the extent of the disease.

pmc-12703207.title: High‐Throughput Sequencings Revealed That Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis is Implicated in Gouty Arthritis of Red‐Crowned Crane (Grus japonensis)
pmc-12703207.creator: Hong Lin, Xiaoyang Zhu, Jianzhong Zhu, Nanhua Chen, Wenbin Bao, Zhong Peng
pmc-12703207.description: The red‐crowned crane (Grus japonensis) is one of the rarest cranes with a global population of less than 4000 individuals. The population of red‐crowned crane could be influenced by health threats, including metabolic and infectious diseases. In the Wildlife Rescue Center of Suining County of Jiangsu Province, gouty arthritis (GA) was observed in all four red‐crowned cranes since March 2024.

pmc-13280734.title: Increased Risk of Injury in Patients with Fabry Disease: A Nationwide Population-Based Cohort Study in Taiwan
pmc-13280734.creator: Chun-Gu Cheng, Yu-Hsuan Chen, Wu-Chien Chien, Hung-Wen Chiu, Fei-Hung Hung, Hung-Pin Peng, Chi-Hsiang Chung, Chun-An Cheng
pmc-13280734.description: BackgroundFabry disease (FD) is a lysosomal storage disorder leading to α-galactosidase A deficiency and glycosphingolipid accumulation. Neurological manifestations of FD, such as central nervous system involvement, peripheral neuropathy, and vestibular dysfunction that results in postural and cognitive impairment, may predispose individuals to injuries. However, the associations between the risk of injury and FD remains underexplored.

pmc-13507064.title: Machine learning-enabled membership determination of open cluster AH03_J0748-26.9 using Gaia DR3 astrometry
pmc-13507064.creator: W. A. Badawy, H. I. Abdel Rahman
pmc-13507064.description: As populations of stars born concurrently, open clusters serve as fundamental laboratories for validating models of star formation, stellar evolution, and the dynamical processes of the Galactic disk. This paper provides a comprehensive astrometric and photometric analysis of the open cluster AH03_J0748-26.9, leveraging data from the Gaia DR3 catalog.

pmc-13655426.title: Long-term lactate ingestion and exercise training differentially modulate body composition, resting substrate metabolism, and tissue-specific metabolic remodeling in mice
pmc-13655426.creator: Inkwon Jang, Nayeon Kim, Deunsol Hwang, Sunghwan Kyun, Taeho Kim, Jungyong Lee, Hun-Young Park, Kiwon Lim, Jisu Kim
pmc-13655426.description: [Purpose] This study investigated whether long-term lactate ingestion induces systemic and tissue-specific metabolic adaptations under normal physiological conditions and whether these responses differ from those induced by exercise training.[Methods] Thirty-two male mice were randomly assigned to saline control, lactate ingestion, exercise training with saline, or exercise training with lactate groups (n = 8/group).
